identity.author: Perpetua, Saturus, and the Redactor
identity.edition: Gebhardt, Acta martyrum selecta (1902), Passio SS. Perpetuae et Felicitatis

sections.locus: Gebhardt VII.VI (Hilarianus; ad bestias; the weaning)
source_text: Alio die cum pranderemus, subito rapti sumus ut audiremur. Et peruenimus ad forum. Rumor statim per uicinas fori partes cucurrit, et factus est populus immensus. Ascendimus in catastam. Interrogati ceteri confessi sunt. Uentum est et ad me. Et apparuit pater ilico cum filio meo, et extraxit me de gradu dicens: Supplica; miserere infanti. Et Hilarianus procurator, qui tunc loco proconsulis Minuci Timiniani defuncti ius gladii acceperat: Parce, inquit, canis patris tui, parce infantiae pueri. Fac sacrum pro salute imperatorum. Et ego respondi: Non facio. Hilarianus: Christiana es? inquit. Et ego respondi: Christiana sum. Et cum staret pater ad me deiciendam, iussus est ab Hilariano proici, et uirga percussus est. Et doluit mihi casus patris mei, quasi ego fuissem percussa: sic dolui pro senecta eius misera. Tunc nos uniuersos pronuntiat et damnat ad bestias; et hilares descendimus ad carcerem. Tunc quia consueuerat a me infans mammas accipere et mecum in carcere manere, statim mitto ad patrem Pomponium diaconum, postulans infantem. Sed pater dare noluit. Et quomodo deus uoluit, neque ille amplius mammas desiderat, neque mihi feruorem fecerunt, ne sollicitudine infantis et dolore mammarum macerarer.
english: Another day, while we were at lunch, we were suddenly hurried off to be heard, and we came to the forum. At once a rumor raced through the quarters around the forum, and an immense crowd formed. We went up onto the platform. The others, when questioned, confessed. My turn too came. And immediately my father appeared with my son, and he pulled me down from the step, saying, Offer the sacrifice; have pity on the child. And Hilarianus the procurator, who had then received the power of the sword in place of the dead proconsul Minucius Timinianus, said, Spare your father's grey hairs, spare the infancy of the boy. Perform the rite for the welfare of the emperors. And I answered, I will not do it. Hilarianus said, Are you a Christian? And I answered, I am a Christian. And while my father stood there to cast me down, he was ordered by Hilarianus to be thrown out, and he was beaten with a rod. And my father's fall pained me, as if I myself had been beaten: so I grieved for his wretched old age. Then he pronounces us all and condemns us to the beasts, and in joy we went down to the prison.

Then, because the child had been accustomed to take the breast from me and to remain with me in the prison, at once I send Pomponius the deacon to my father, asking for the child. But my father would not give him. And as God willed it, the child no longer craved the breast, nor did my breasts become inflamed, so that I should not be worn away by anxiety for the child and by pain in the breasts.
